author: Nick Koutsobinas
title: Social Security Administration Announces Anti-Fraud Check for Claims
text:
• The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced plans for an 'anti-fraud check' on claims filed by phone.
• The anti-fraud checks will begin on April 14, 2025.
• Claims filed over the telephone will be flagged if they have fraud risk indicators.
• The announcement follows findings of waste, fraud, and abuse by the Department of Government Efficiency.
• Issues include noncitizens receiving Social Security numbers and payments to accounts that are '100, 200 and even 300 years old.'
• Individuals whose accounts are flagged will need to prove their identity in person.
• If no fraud is detected, individuals can continue processing their claims online.
• The SSA conducts 100 percent ID proofing for all in-person claims.
• Approximately 4.5 million telephone claims are made each year, with an estimated 70,000 potentially flagged.
• Last month, the SSA announced that identity verification over the phone would no longer be allowed, but later reversed this decision, stating phone verification remains an option.
